reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the ChargeItem resource report, the supplied resource-review context, the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level conclusion, and the direct SearchParameters/HttpRestBehavior findings whose affectedResources include ChargeItem. Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because ChargeItem is neither Resource nor DomainResource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 ChargeItem was trial-use/FMM 0, so the baseline compatibility expectation is weak and broad production prevalence should not be assumed. The low maturity does not erase impact entirely because the removed resource represents billing, reimbursement, and audit facts, but it lowers the burden for accepting substantial redesign if a coherent R6 replacement strategy exists.

overall.oneLineConclusion: ChargeItem's absence from the R6 core package makes resource-level migration unavoidable; the key standards question is the transition or successor mapping, not preserving derivative codegen, REST, or search surfaces by themselves.

reasoning.thesisMd: ChargeItem is not a mostly stable resource with a few local R4-to-R6 breaks. R4 defines a concrete DomainResource specialization with required `status`, `code`, and `subject`; the supplied R6 ballot core package has no computable `ChargeItem` StructureDefinition, package-index row, resource-type code, OpenAPI definition, or same-identity search surface. That is a resource identity break, so implementers with persisted or exchanged ChargeItem instances need a migration program before R6 validation or native R6 APIs can work.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is removed-or-replaced-resource rather than a rename of a few fields. Candidate nearby R6 surfaces are not lossless: `Invoice.lineItem.chargeItem[x]` can carry a code or unprofiled reference but does not preserve the standalone charge-event lifecycle, performer, occurrence, organization, account, override, service/product, note, and supporting-information model; `DeviceDefinition.chargeItem` is catalog metadata rather than a patient/event charge record. Real migration therefore requires policy decisions about whether data becomes invoice-line content, extensions, legacy/versioned resources, or an external financial-system object.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the resource identity itself is gone, preventing additional ChargeItem-specific breaks has reduced independent leverage. Generated classes, REST endpoint advertisements, and ChargeItem search parameters cannot be preserved as native R6 conformance surfaces without also retaining or replacing the resource. This does not mean compatibility preservation has no value: the resource-removal decision and the absence of an explicit successor or transition mapping remain standards-review-worthy. It means the useful compatibility lever is a coherent transition resource/mapping strategy, not isolated preservation of derivative surfaces after removal is accepted.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The plausible less-breaking base option is to retain ChargeItem as deprecated/legacy trial-use content for one release, or publish a first-class successor plus explicit mappings and endpoint/search transition guidance. That could preserve many R4 instances and generated surfaces, but it is not a trivial low-cost alias: it keeps an FMM 0 financial event model in core, creates possible duplicate representations with Invoice, and requires continued validation/API/search support. If the work group intentionally retired the model, implementation shims and versioned legacy endpoints are mitigations, not base R6 compatibility preservation.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings for ChargeItem are real but derivative. R4 ChargeItem endpoint discoverability and ChargeItem-only search parameters disappear because there is no R6 ChargeItem endpoint or base resource. Those matter for migration planning and conformance tooling, but they do not independently justify preserving search or REST surfaces unless a ChargeItem successor or legacy endpoint is also preserved. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation and meta/search changes may affect ChargeItem instances in generic workflows, but they are not resource-specific evidence for this ChargeItem conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate's headline conclusion is directionally right: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable=Yes`, `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and `migration-program-dominates`. My independent review adds two qualifications: low R4 maturity weakens the presumption that the old model must be preserved, while the billing/audit semantics and residual Invoice ChargeItem wording mean the removal and mapping gap still deserve standards attention rather than being dismissed as a local migration chore.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high about the observed package absence and resulting validation/API break. Confidence is lower about HL7 intent because the local inputs did not include an official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot rationale, Jira history, rendered financial-module guidance, or final R6 package. The R6 input is a ballot build, so final publication could change the resource disposition.

findingConsiderations.title: ChargeItem resource is absent from the R6 ballot core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the dominant resource-level fact: an R4 `ChargeItem` instance has no same-name R6 StructureDefinition or native validation target. FMM 0 lowers stability pressure, but whole-resource removal in a billing/audit domain still deserves explicit rationale and transition guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: No lossless R6 destination for ChargeItem billing-event fields was found
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding shows the migration is not a mechanical move into Invoice or DeviceDefinition. It is standards-review-worthy because implementers need human policy decisions for lifecycle state, subject, occurrence, performers, overrides, account allocation, service/product links, notes, and supporting information.

findingConsiderations.title: ChargeItem-specific generated models, schemas, REST/search surfaces, and resource-type switches disappear
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real operational migration chore for generated SDKs, schemas, resource-type switches, and route registration. It is mostly a consequence of the identity removal, so it should not be treated as an independent avoidable break unless ChargeItem itself is retained or replaced.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For ChargeItem, old searches such as ChargeItem-specific patient, code, account, occurrence, performer, quantity, service, or subject queries have no native R6 base endpoint. Transition aliases could help only if the standard also defines a legacy endpoint or clear successor mapping.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The ChargeItem REST endpoint disappearance affects generic clients and conformance tooling, but it is derivative of the removed resource. The practical next step is documenting the ChargeItem disposition rather than preserving an endpoint advertisement with no R6 resource definition.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This may affect generic Resource-level workflows that once operated on ChargeItem instances, but it is a shared Resource behavior issue and is not evidence that changes to the ChargeItem resource model itself are more or less acceptable.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource search metadata change is relevant background for generic clients, but it is not ChargeItem-specific and should not be counted as a direct ChargeItem migration driver.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Ask the responsible work group to confirm whether ChargeItem was intentionally retired, accidentally omitted from the ballot package, or replaced by another artifact, and publish explicit R4-to-R6 disposition guidance.

If ChargeItem removal is intentional, provide a normative or ballot-visible migration map for the event-level fields that do not fit cleanly into `Invoice.lineItem.chargeItem[x]` or `DeviceDefinition.chargeItem`, including guidance for status, occurrence, performers, organizations, overrides, accounts, service/product links, notes, and supporting information.

Consider a deprecated legacy ChargeItem resource, explicit successor resource, or documented endpoint/search aliases only if the work group wants base R6 to preserve R4 instances or native API compatibility during transition.

For implementers, inventory all persisted ChargeItem data, generated model references, REST routes, search queries, and validation rules before upgrading; most breakage is a planned resource migration rather than a set of independent per-field fixes.

caveats: The R6 input is 6.0.0-ballot4; final R6 publication may restore, replace, or further document ChargeItem.
No official change rationale or financial-module migration guide was available in the local inputs.
R4 ChargeItem is trial-use/FMM 0, so the review should not infer broad production prevalence from the existence of the resource alone.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context and not scored as ChargeItem-specific breaks.
